steps.thought: I will list the available tests on the manufacturing line to determine the station test capabilities and costs.

tests.name: power_on_selftest
tests.description: Boot the unit and enumerate devices on I2C, UART and CAN.

tests.name: battery_rest_check
tests.description: Read pack and per-cell voltages at rest.

tests.name: esc_telemetry
tests.description: Read ESC telemetry: sync errors, packet loss, back-EMF detection.

tests.name: compass_static
tests.description: Compare compass heading to the fixture reference with motors off.

tests.name: harness_continuity
tests.description: Measure per-bus continuity resistance and CAN termination.

tests.name: camera_selftest
tests.description: Run camera built-in self test and measure frame rate and CSI errors.

tests.name: imu_static
tests.description: Log 1000 IMU samples on the static fixture: gyro bias, accel noise, dropouts.

tests.name: motor_spin_test
tests.description: Spin all motors at 50 percent throttle: current, RPM, RPM jitter, temp.

tests.name: compass_motor_interference
tests.description: Sweep throttle 0-75 percent and log compass heading deviation.

tests.name: battery_load_test
tests.description: Apply a 20 A load and measure sag, cell imbalance, internal resistance.

steps.thought: I will run power_on_selftest as the first diagnostic step to quickly check the fundamental boot health and device enumeration across I2C, UART, and CAN.
steps.observation: The power-on selftest completed with a failure in reading the camera sensor ID, while all other buses and devices enumerated successfully.

hypotheses.rationale: Camera sensor ID read failed during boot, which is commonly caused by a loose or damaged camera CSI ribbon cable.
The camera sensor failed to communicate its ID during power-on, pointing to either a ribbon fault or a dead sensor.

steps.thought: I will run the camera selftest to check if the camera sensor responds or if there are frame rate and CSI errors, which will distinguish between a ribbon cable fault and a dead camera sensor.
steps.observation: The camera selftest confirms that the sensor ID is not readable and the frame rate is 0 fps, directly pointing to a camera hardware or cabling failure.

hypotheses.rationale: Failure to read camera sensor ID along with 0 fps framerate strongly points to a disconnected or damaged CSI ribbon cable.
Complete lack of communication and zero frame rate could also be caused by a dead camera sensor module.

steps.thought: We need to determine if the camera ribbon cable is at fault or if the entire camera module is dead. Since no further camera tests exist, we can proceed to propose the rework for the most common cause of camera sensor non-responsiveness: the ribbon cable.
steps.observation: Rework applied; full suite passed: False.
